title: Oracle-blind review of export portability, operations documentation, and rollback
rationale: The export implementation reopens and unlinks a NamedTemporaryFile while its handle is open, a known Windows failure pattern. Evidence covers Linux only, the documentation changes the stated freshness default without a corresponding runtime change in the supplied patches, and the required isolated rollback rehearsal remains not run.
scope_architecture: The export helper is an operational software path and the operations document defines operator-visible behavior. The changes remain in their nominal owners, but the implementation is not portable to a supported operating system and the documented default is not backed by a runtime/configuration patch.

findings.finding: The export path reopens and deletes a named temporary file while its original handle remains open.
findings.evidence: 09-windows-path.diff performs Path.write_text and Path.unlink inside the NamedTemporaryFile context.
findings.evidence_excerpt:
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() as handle:
    Path(handle.name).write_text(payload, encoding="utf-8")
    Path(handle.name).unlink()
findings.impact: Windows file-locking semantics can raise an access or cleanup error, breaking the required export path on a supported CI platform.
findings.required_change: Close the temporary file before reopening or deleting it, use a cross-platform temporary-path pattern, and make cleanup idempotent.
findings.suggested_test: Test successful export and cleanup on Windows and Linux with all file handles explicitly closed before deletion.

findings.finding: The automated evidence covers Linux but does not include the required Windows execution and cleanup check.
findings.evidence: The supplied CI statement names Linux and documentation checks only.
findings.evidence_excerpt: PASS: CI on Linux and documentation checks
findings.impact: A platform-specific file-locking regression can be reported as fully green without ever exercising the failing operating system.
findings.required_change: Run the focused export and cleanup tests on both Windows and Linux and record both outcomes.
findings.suggested_test: Run the export test matrix on Windows and Linux and verify the temporary path no longer exists after explicit close.

findings.finding: The required isolated rollback rehearsal is not run even though approval is requested.
findings.evidence: The supplied manual evidence explicitly leaves rollback pending.
findings.impact: Operators have no observed proof that rollback restores export behavior, health, and data integrity after the availability-affecting change.
findings.required_change: Complete the isolated rollback rehearsal and record the candidate identity, abort boundary, rollback owner, post-rollback health, and data checks.
findings.suggested_test: manual: Rehearse rollback in an isolated project and verify export behavior, service health, and representative data before and after rollback.

findings.finding: Operations documentation changes the stated freshness default from 300 seconds to 30 seconds without a corresponding runtime or configuration change in the supplied patches.
findings.evidence: 10-docs-manual.diff changes only the documented value for the freshness default.
findings.evidence_excerpt:
State freshness defaults to 300 seconds.
State freshness defaults to 30 seconds.
findings.impact: Operators can diagnose stale state, tune alerts, or execute rollback against a threshold that does not match deployable behavior.
findings.required_change: Restore the documented 300-second default or include and verify the approved runtime/configuration change to 30 seconds across all consumers.
findings.suggested_test: Verify the documented freshness default against the rendered runtime configuration and its focused behavior test.

contract_consumer_review: The export helper is consumed by supported Windows and Linux workflows, but only Linux evidence is supplied. The freshness default is an operator-visible configuration contract; the documentation patch changes that claim without a matching runtime producer or consumer update.

evidence_matrix.check: PASS: CI on Linux and documentation checks

operations_safety_security_privacy: The export failure is a supported-platform availability defect. The requested approval is premature because rollback has not been rehearsed, and the operator-facing freshness value is inconsistent with the supplied implementation scope. No destructive action or production access was performed.
documentation_assessment: The operations document changes a runtime-default claim without matching code/configuration evidence. The implementation report also requests approval while recording the mandatory rollback rehearsal as not run, so the documented readiness claim is not supportable.
limitations: Review was limited to 09-windows-path.diff, 10-docs-manual.diff, and the two supplied evidence statements.
The isolated rollback rehearsal was not performed because it is explicitly reported as not run.
